req.title: Redirect-to accepts POST as well
req.statement: The system shall accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE on /redirect-to.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the /redirect-to endpoint should accept multiple HTTP methods including POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE, and return a 2xx response with the expected payload. The tests are designed to verify this functionality by checking positive, negative, and boundary cases.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_method
actions: Send a POST request to /redirect-to with a valid URL.
expected: The Location header matches the provided URL.
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()
response = client.post('/redirect-to', data={'url': 'http://example.com'})
assert response.status_code == 302
assert response.headers['Location'] == b'http://example.com'

tests.name: test_redirect_to_invalid_method
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()
response = client.head('/redirect-to')
assert response.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_status_code
actions: Send a GET request to /redirect-to with a status_code of 299.
expected: The Location header matches the provided URL.
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()
response = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=299')
assert response.status_code == 302
assert response.headers['Location'] == b'http://example.com'
